title: How a roof keeps water out
caption: Every layer on your roof has one job 🏠🌧️ #howitsbuilt #roofing #homeowner #construction #howitworks

lines.text: If your roof were just flat boards, every rainstorm would drip right onto your bed.
So you tilt the roof, so rain runs off instead of sitting on top.
But wood soaks up water and rots.
So you cover the boards with *underlayment*, a waterproof sheet that's the roof's backup layer.
But the sun cooks it, and wind rips it up.
So you nail on *shingles*, starting at the bottom and overlapping each row like fish scales.
Water runs down over each one and never gets underneath.
And each row hides the nails of the row below.
But water curls under the bottom edge and soaks the wood.
So a metal *drip edge* makes it fall off cleanly into the gutter.
In winter, melted snow refreezes at the edge into an *ice dam*, and the water behind it backs up under the shingles.
So the bottom few feet get a sticky membrane called *ice and water shield*.
And wherever the roof meets a chimney, there's a gap.
So you bend metal *flashing* into the corner and tuck it under the shingles.
But the attic traps hot, damp air that can rot the roof from the inside.
So vents at the bottom edge and a *ridge vent* at the top let fresh air flow through.
